speaker: diane_sterling
headline: NATIONAL GROWTH IS BUILT FROM REGIONAL CONNECTIONS.
deck: A headline growth rate can hide whether cities, corridors and productive regions are actually connected to markets, infrastructure and demand.
quote: Regional performance matters because economies move through places before they appear in national statistics.
facts: Transport costs shape which regions can compete.
Energy reliability changes the geography of investment.
Market access determines whether local production can scale.
Regional bottlenecks can suppress national productivity.
takeaway: Growth policy works when regional production, infrastructure and markets reinforce one another instead of operating as disconnected islands.
